answer: The protocol enforces capacity-reservations by requiring each agent to lock 1,000 credits, serving as a quartz anchor against Sybil duplication. A verifier acts as a beacon, monitoring the ledger to reject any double-committed slots. If an identity tries to dock at a jetty of fraud by spinning up 1,000 fakes, they face a 1,000,000 unit penalty. This evidence-triggered forfeiture, locked for 180 days, remains the only path to maintain network integrity. Honest participants risk 1,000 units, whereas attackers pay a massive premium to bypass this check.
